page: Microsoft Azure E2pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors running at 3.0 GHz, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs without multithreading overhead. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware package also integrates 81 GB of local SSD temporary storage and operates under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, without attached GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show that single-core capabilities outpace overall multi-core throughput due to the low core count. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 1791.39, ranking in the middle tier, whereas multi-core execution reached 3552.48, placing in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth metrics yield 27.08 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 16.68 GB/sec for writes. Geekbench results confirm modest compute capability, producing 1107.0 in single-core and 1978.0 in multi-core evaluation, with specialized sub-tests like software compilation and ray tracing registering in the lowest tier.

Operationally, the ARM-based Ampere architecture provides power and density efficiency for scale-out applications, but computational limitations represent a clear tradeoff. Intensive mathematical modeling, code compilation, and LLM inference run slowly, as evidenced by small-model LLM generation rates reaching only 28.01 tokens per second. However, with 2.8 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and stable static web throughput of 2.91 GB/sec, the instance provides steady memory access for lightweight deployments.

Microsoft Azure E2pds_v5 is primarily suited for memory-sensitive, low-compute workloads. These include mid-tier in-memory caching nodes, small Redis or database instances, lightweight web serving layers, and ARM-native staging environments that require a high RAM-to-core allocation without intense computational demands.
